source_snapshot.test_set: Intel GNR CPU RAS - SMBus Hang Recovery
source_snapshot.purpose_facts: Configure Intel GNR error-injection and SMI recovery settings, halt the target through CScripts, verify I3C-controller `intr_status.transfer_err_stat` bit 9 is clear, inject I3C HALT error type 0x13 at socket 0/SPDI3C 0, verify bit 9 sets, resume the target and confirm serial-log bus recovery.
procedure_facts: Apply a large Intel-reference EDKII/CScripts, ELOG, WHEA, error-injection, firmware-first and crash-log configuration plus `Smbus Error Recovery = SMI`.
Use `halt()` and `ei.utils.resetInjectorLockCheck()` in the CScripts harness.
Require injection success and bit 9 set, then call `go()` and inspect serial output for I3C bus recovery.
criteria_facts: Serial output shows I3C bus recovery.
source_conflicts: The item/test-set call the test SMBus Hang Recovery while every injection target, register path, error description and recovery criterion identifies an I3C controller/bus.
The source does not explain whether `Smbus Error Recovery = SMI` is intended to recover a legacy I2C/SMBus device on an I3C-capable controller or whether the title is stale.
The long reference BIOS list is not scoped to the minimum settings actually required for this single injection, and several unlock/debug settings materially alter platform security/error handling.
missing_source_information: Intel/ODM recipe version proving the SMBus/I3C relationship, expected SMI handler and exact serial recovery signature.
Signed target map for socket 0, compute 0, SPDI3C 0 and controller register bit 9.
CScripts/harness and silicon/BIOS compatibility, exact `halt()`/`go()` target-control semantics and injection success output.
Expected post-recovery bit-9 state, bus/device health checks, timeout, reset escalation and required BIOS/GRUB restoration matrix.

original_test_intent.statement: Exercise the platform-defined SMI recovery path for an Intel GNR SPDI3C/I3C-controller HALT fault by proving a clean pre-state, injecting error type 0x13 at the specified controller, proving transfer error bit 9 asserts, resuming the halted target and correlating the expected serial recovery event with restored bus/platform health.
must_preserve: Intel GNR platform and the exact signed socket/compute/SPDI3C/controller target.
`Smbus Error Recovery = SMI` and the approved minimal prerequisite configuration.
CScripts target halt, injector-lock reset and later resume semantics.
Pre-injection bit 9 clear and post-injection bit 9 set observations.
Exactly one error type 0x13 injection and serial recovery proof.
must_not_infer: That `halt()` is the Linux OS halt command or that `go()` is an OS shell command.
That generic `smbus`, `i2c`, `hang` or `recovery` text proves this controller recovered.
That I3C backward compatibility alone resolves the source's SMBus-versus-I3C naming conflict.
That bit 9 assertion is recovery rather than injected-error evidence.
That every reference BIOS knob is safe, available or necessary on the ODM BIOS.

v2_review_conclusion.summary: V2 correctly retains the concrete I3C HALT sequence as conditionally executable, flags the SMBus/I3C scope mismatch, requires exact target/harness approval and refuses to rely on generic dmesg/SEL matches.
v2_review_conclusion.specific_gap: V2 does not explicitly distinguish CScripts `halt()`/`go()` target-control calls from OS power commands, and it does not require the owner to state which BIOS/GRUB changes are actually necessary or the expected post-recovery register/bus state. Those gaps can cause execution on the wrong control plane or leave debug settings enabled.

related_records: Other Intel error-injection cases do not establish this controller's err_type 0x13 semantics, bit-9 behavior or SMI recovery signature.
applicable_history.precedence_application: Preserve the explicit register/injector sequence as the executable fact, but retain SOURCE_CONFLICT for the SMBus title versus I3C procedure. Public I3C compatibility information cannot substitute for the missing Intel/ODM recovery recipe.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Keep the approval-gated classification and exact I3C HALT mechanics, but require the owner to resolve what SMBus recovery means on this I3C controller and to define the minimal BIOS/GRUB change set, serial signature and post-recovery health. `halt()` and `go()` remain harness target-control operations, never host shutdown/resume commands.

conditions_present: Platform family, candidate target, pre/post fault bit, injection API/error type, recovery policy setting, target-control sequence and serial evidence channel are supplied.
missing: Scope resolution, signed target/register/error semantics, harness compatibility, minimal BIOS/GRUB delta, expected injection and serial signatures, post-recovery bit/bus health, timeout and recovery.
provider: Intel FAE/ODM firmware owner supplies the versioned injection/recovery recipe, target map, exact signatures and required settings.
BIOS owner maps reference paths to the shipping BIOS and supplies restore values.
Lab owner approves the disruptive window, serial/OOB observation and reset/recovery.
safe_read_only_work: Record CPU stepping, BIOS/BMC/OS/kernel and harness identities and current BIOS/GRUB setting matrix.
Resolve socket/compute/SPDI3C/controller topology and collect serial/SEL/OS baselines without clearing them.
Inspect the target register only through the approved harness read path before injection and preserve the full value.
prohibited_until_resolved: Changing BIOS/GRUB settings, calling harness `halt()`, resetting injector locks, injecting 0x13, using Linux `halt`, running generic substitute injectors, resuming/rebooting/resetting, clearing logs or claiming PASS.
closure_evidence: Recipe explicitly reconciles SMBus naming with the I3C controller/legacy path and maps bit 9 plus the expected SMI recovery handler.
Signed minimal settings delta, harness version/target, expected success output, serial event and post-recovery state are available.
Baseline bit 9 is clear and serial/OOB reset plus complete settings restoration are ready before approval.

revision_candidate.test_name: Validate SMI Recovery from an Intel GNR SPDI3C/I3C HALT Injection
revision_candidate.purpose: Validate the owner-defined SMBus-compatible or I3C bus recovery path by injecting exactly one HALT error type 0x13 into the mapped Intel GNR SPDI3C controller, observing the `transfer_err_stat` field at bit 9 of the same controller's `intr_status` register (`intr_status.transfer_err_stat[9]`) transition from clear to set, resuming target execution and proving the expected SMI-driven serial recovery event and restored bus/platform health.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: Only the Intel GNR stepping, BIOS/EDKII build, CScripts/error-injection harness, SPDI3C topology and SMI recovery implementation in the signed Intel/ODM recipe. `halt()` and `go()` execute inside that harness against the validated target; they are not Linux host commands.
revision_candidate.target_scope: One mapped socket 0 / compute 0 / SPDI3C 0 / `sb_i3c_0` controller and one err_type 0x13 injection. The recovery claim is limited to the bus/controller and legacy SMBus/I2C relation explicitly documented by the owner. It does not cover other sockets/controllers or generic SMBus recovery. Treat 30/30 minutes as estimates.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: CPU/board/firmware identity; signed Intel/ODM recipe resolving SMBus versus I3C scope; CScripts/harness version and credentials; exact target map confirming that `sv.socket0.compute0.uncore.spdi3cbus.spdi3cbus0.sb_i3c_0.intr_status.transfer_err_stat[9]` is the authoritative field for this injection, plus error-type semantics; minimal ODM BIOS and GRUB prerequisite plus original/restore values; `Smbus Error Recovery = SMI` implementation; expected injector success and timestamped serial recovery signature; expected post-recovery value/clear behavior of that same field plus bus/device health rule; serial/OOB access; baseline logs; timeout; one-attempt authorization; reset/BIOS recovery and evidence storage.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Capture identities, complete current settings and serial/SEL/OS baseline, then apply only the signed BIOS/GRUB delta and reboot if required. In the approved CScripts console, map the target, call harness `halt()` once and `ei.utils.resetInjectorLockCheck()`, read the full `sv.socket0.compute0.uncore.spdi3cbus.spdi3cbus0.sb_i3c_0.intr_status` register and require its `transfer_err_stat` field at bit 9 to be clear. After explicit approval, run exactly `ei.sys.injectI3CError(socket=0, spdi3c=0, err_type=0x13)`, preserve the full result and reread that identical register/field to require `intr_status.transfer_err_stat[9]` set. Call harness `go()` once, correlate the exact timestamped serial recovery signature to this target/injection, collect the prescribed post-recovery value of the same register/field plus bus/device/platform health, and restore every changed BIOS/GRUB/debug setting with verification.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Dedicated non-production SUT; exact CPU/firmware/harness/target match; owner-resolved SMBus/I3C semantics; signed minimal settings and restore matrix applied; serial/OOB and reset recovery proven; baseline bit 9 clear; bus/devices/platform healthy; no competing fault injection; stable power; evidence capture active; one-shot approval immediately before target halt/injection.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Platform/firmware/harness/recipe identities; signed scope and target map; before/applied/restored BIOS/GRUB settings; full pre-injection `sb_i3c_0.intr_status` with its `transfer_err_stat[9]` field clear; target-halt and injector-lock-reset transcript; exact 0x13 injection command, success response and timestamp; full post-injection read of that same register with the same field set; `go()` transcript; exact correlated serial SMI/recovery signature; owner-defined post-recovery value of the same register/field and bus/device/platform health; SEL/dmesg/serial deltas; no unrelated fatal condition; verified settings restoration; engineer disposition.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The signed Intel/ODM GNR injection/recovery recipe for the exact controller and firmware. Pass requires correct target, a clean `intr_status.transfer_err_stat[9]` pre-state, one successful 0x13 injection, assertion of that identical field, target resume, exact correlated recovery signature, the prescribed post-recovery value of that same field, all bus/device/platform checks and complete settings restoration. A generic log match, injector return alone or bit assertion alone is insufficient.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Do not run on production, translate harness calls into OS halt/resume, guess the controller, broaden to other sockets, substitute an SMBus/I2C injector, change unapproved BIOS/GRUB settings, clear evidence logs, inject when bit 9 is already set, repeat automatically, call `go()`/reset outside the signed sequence or leave DFX/locks/error-injection settings altered. Stop on target mismatch, unexpected register value, harness error, lost serial/OOB, bus lock, fatal/crash, missing exact recovery signature, device/platform degradation or restore failure.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Intel/ODM owner approves scope, recipe, target, signatures and settings; BIOS owner approves unlock/debug changes and restoration; lab owner approves the disruptive one-shot injection and recovery; a human authorizes halt/injection immediately before execution and judges PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED or any reset/retry.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Humans/FAE supply protected CScripts, map ODM BIOS paths, authorize disruptive state changes and handle exceptional reset/recovery. An Agent may drive the exact approved harness sequence and evidence capture after handoff, but may not resolve the SMBus/I3C conflict, invent signatures, self-authorize injection or retry.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: On harness, register, bus, crash or serial failure, stop further calls, preserve all evidence and use only the signed serial/OOB reset or BIOS recovery. Verify target bus/devices, BMC and host health, then restore every changed BIOS/GRUB/DFX/lock setting. No rerun is allowed until the owner reviews the failure and issues fresh approval.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: SMBus/I3C scope, authoritative `intr_status.transfer_err_stat[9]` mapping, recipe/harness compatibility, minimal settings/restore matrix, expected injection/serial/post-recovery state, approval, timeout or recovery is missing; platform identity differs; that field is not clear at baseline; target halt/reset-lock check fails; injection returns unexpected status; that same field does not set after injection; exact recovery event is absent or uncorrelated; bus/device/BMC/host health degrades; fatal/crash persists; or settings cannot be restored.

identified_defects: The title/test-set say SMBus while the executable target and criteria are I3C-specific.
The source does not define whether an I3C controller's legacy compatibility path is the intended SMBus scope.
Harness `halt()`/`go()` can be dangerously confused with host OS commands.
The reference BIOS list is broader than a proven minimum and contains security/error-handling changes.
Expected serial signature, post-recovery bit state and bus/device health are absent.
reason_for_change: Retain V2's safe conditional execution while making the harness control plane, unresolved SMBus/I3C relationship, minimal settings delta and recovery-completion evidence explicit enough to prevent wrong-command execution or generic-log PASS.

new_technical_evidence.title: I3C protocol
new_technical_evidence.applicability: General protocol context only, not proof of this Intel controller implementation
new_technical_evidence.supports: I3C is designed for backward compatibility with I2C devices and may host mixed device types, so SMBus/I2C naming around an I3C controller is technically possible; however that general fact does not identify this test's recovery path.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: Only the Intel/ODM recipe can prove whether err_type 0x13 and SMI recovery exercise the title's intended SMBus path.

new_technical_evidence.title: I3C master controller driver API
new_technical_evidence.supports: An I3C master controller can expose an I2C adapter for backward compatibility, reinforcing that controller identity, legacy-path mapping and recovery evidence must be platform-specific rather than inferred from a label.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The source uses an Intel debug harness/register path, not the Linux driver API.

new_technical_evidence.title: Source testcase Wistron-System RAS-00116-V002
new_technical_evidence.supports: The exact BIOS setting, harness target, bit-9 pre/post checks, error type 0x13, target resume and serial I3C recovery criterion.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The SMBus title relationship, signatures, minimum settings and final state are absent.

removed_ambiguities: Defines `halt()` and `go()` as CScripts target-control operations, not OS commands.
Keeps SMBus/I3C reconciliation as a source conflict instead of assuming protocol compatibility resolves it.
Separates bit-9 error assertion from actual recovery proof.
Requires a minimal settings/restore matrix and an exact correlated serial event.
resolved_blockers: The case is not permanently BLOCKED: a versioned harness, target map and Intel/ODM recipe can close the current handoff gaps and permit controlled automation.
remaining_blockers: Execution awaits scope reconciliation, harness/target semantics, minimal BIOS/GRUB delta, expected signatures/post-state, approval and recovery.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 prevents the most dangerous interpretation error—running target-debug `halt()`/`go()` as host commands—and makes recovery depend on the exact controller-correlated SMI event, post-health and restored security/debug settings rather than a generic log match.

agent_understanding_result.notes: The first contract-only validation found `transfer_err_stat bit 9` versus `intr_status bit 9` could be read as competing registers. V3 was revised to use the fully qualified `sb_i3c_0.intr_status.transfer_err_stat[9]` consistently for pre-injection, post-injection and owner-defined post-recovery reads. Revalidation confirmed the register/field relationship and found no remaining document defect.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: Reliability row 159 sets Smbus Error Recovery to SMI but injects Intel I3C HALT error type 0x13 into socket0/SPDI3C0, observes intr_status bit 9 and requires serial I3C recovery after harness `go()`.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 correctly gates the scope conflict but does not make the target-debug meaning of halt/go or the missing minimum settings and post-recovery register/health contract explicit.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Allow identity, settings, topology and register baseline collection; permit one exact harness injection only after the owner reconciles scope and supplies signatures, minimal settings, recovery and restoration.
